transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lindsey Park (Redwood CSM), Diego Morales (Aurelia SRE), Priya Shah (Aurelia Platform Eng), Markus Engel (Aurelia CTO), Hanna Li (Aurelia Tech Lead)
Links shared: incident-runbook-v2.docx, bench-results-sept3.csv, gc-eviction-proposal.md, dedicated-quote.pdf

Summary (auto): quick rehearsal of runbook, clarify who flips canary, short-term Dedicated pilot discussed, agreement to run bench with real payloads, action owners assigned.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok everyone thanks for joining on short notice uh we'll do a sharp 45, 50 minute run through of the recovery steps from last week, Diego can you give us the quick 60 second what-you-saw in prod?
[00:18] Diego: yeah sure, so on Sept third around 02:12 UTC we started seeing token queues creep up, at first latency went from ~90ms to about 400ms then at 02:25 we saw request pile-up and a number of in-flight kv cache misses, it kinda propagated into backpressure across the path, eventually we hit the autoscale ceiling and then retries made it worse, uh the root signal looked like a sustained increase in sequence length and a weird GC stall on the runtime host.
[00:45] Maya: when you say GC stall is that, is that OS level or the runtime heap?
[00:52] Diego: it seemed like the runtime heap — we observed long pauses in the process, memory worked up to like 93 percent on the node, and the eviction policy didn't free the KV entries fast enough. there might also be a leak in our prompt concatenation logic but that's speculative.
[01:12] Priya: on our side we had a concurrency bump for a new customer feature which pushed more large prompts; we didn't anticipate that interleaving with long context tokens would push KV retention so high.
[01:28] Ravi: hmm ok. from Redwood's side we looked at the traces and there were a couple of key contributors — one is the eviction threshold was tuned for average use not the 99th percentile burst; second is the GC fallback path when memory pressure hits peak was slower because of a lock contention path in the older runtime build you were on.
[01:50] Hanna: so is this the same thing as the KV overflow issue we saw in staging a month ago, or different?
[01:58] Ravi: related but not identical. Staging hit the overflow on a synthetic workload. Prod was compounded by request retries and a sequence-length shift. also the model variant pushed more kv usage per request.
[02:18] Markus: we're concerned about repeat exposure; our team needs a deterministic way to bring service back without manual intervention.
[02:25] Lindsey: absolutely and that's the goal of the rehearsal today — run the steps in the runbook and make sure ownership and timings are clear.
[02:34] Maya: ok quick agenda: (1) RCA cliff notes (2) runbook steps and handoffs (3) hotfix vs rollback tradeoffs (4) pilot Dedicated buffer and telemetry gating (5) next steps. sound good?
[02:46] Customer: yes

--- RCA deep-dive ---
[03:10] Ravi: we ran the flamegraphs, the biggest time sinks were kv-lookup lock waits and a safepoint during nested GC; the older kernel path has a stop-the-world region we see on the runtime 1.6 build. we recommend two short term mitigations: raise eviction aggressiveness for large keys and backport a GC lock fix into a 1.6.3 runtime hotfix.
[03:40] Priya: is the eviction change safe for correctness? we worry about dropping useful cache entries and increasing latency.
[03:47] Ravi: good question — the proposed policy is size-first but with a short TTL bump for prefixes; effectively small hot keys stay, large old keys are removed faster. it should actually reduce p99 latency by reducing memory pressure. we'll add a feature flag so you can revert quickly.
[04:05] Diego: what's the rollback path if the hotfix creates regressions?
[04:08] Ravi: rollback is a traffic diversion to the previous runtime version and a short-lived Dedicated route we can spin up as a buffer. that is why Maya's pricing memo for a 48h Dedicated buffer matters.
[04:20] Maya: yes I'll share options after the call — two week commit or a short 48 hour trial we bill differently.

--- Runbook rehearsal ---
[05:00] Lindsey: step one, detect signal: increase in token_queue_length metric above threshold X for 3 minutes. step two, auto-notify on-call and open incident. step three, enable eviction aggressive flag and monitor p95/p99 for 10 minutes. step four if no improvement, flip canary to 1.6.3-hotfix or divert to Dedicated buffer. step five, postmortem and customer comms.
[05:35] Hanna: who has authority to flip the canary?
[05:38] Lindsey: on the Redwood side the SE oncall (Ravi) flips; customer side SRE (Diego) approves and we do the change together. we need an approval TTL so it's not blocked.
[05:50] Diego: ok agreed. we want automated guardrails though — if p50 drops and p99 still high maybe automated diversion?
[05:58] Ravi: we can build an automated fallback policy but we need to agree thresholds; automation may cause oscillation so we recommend manual first for two rehearsals then consider automation.

--- Hotfix vs Rollback tradeoffs ---
[06:30] Ravi: hotfix advantage: fixes lock contention without changing model; lower blast radius if feature flag present. downside: shipping new runtime build under pressure. rollback advantage: already vetted runtime version, quick to switch, but you lose any fixes and may have capacity constraints.
[06:50] Markus: if we divert to Dedicated, what's the latency delta?
[06:54] Maya: Dedicated in our tests had p95 ~160ms on similar workloads, hosted was 110ms normally; Dedicated buffer loses a bit on tail but buys isolation. pricing is per-hour+tokens.
[07:10] Priya: ok we don't love the latency hit but prefer predictable behavior over noisy production.

--- Telemetry and auditability ---
[07:40] Lindsey: we also discussed audit logs — who flipped flags, who approved diversions, and KMS usage for any keys in private deployment. we will attach an audit log entry to every manual intervention.
[07:52] Diego: we need SSO mapped roles so only our oncall can approve diversions; can you route SAML group to that action?
[07:58] Ravi: yes we support SAML/SCIM mapping to roles, we'll work with your IdP team.

--- Pilot plan ---
[08:20] Maya: proposed pilot: spin up a 2-node Dedicated pool for 48 hours with same model and run replay of incident payloads. we'll run benched load until we replicate degradation criteria; if mitigation holds we'll then test autoscale threshold changes.
[08:36] Diego: timeline?
[08:38] Maya: aim to start bench on 9/10, results same day or 9/11.
[08:44] Priya: we can provide logs and a subset of traffic for replay, and we'll sign off on a time window.

--- Questions and concerns ---
[09:05] Hanna: we noticed some mis-labeled spans in the trace where model-id was obfuscated as 'unknown-1' — will that be fixed?
[09:12] Ravi: yes that's a tracing tagging bug; small change to the exporter will be in the hotfix PR.
[09:18] Diego: any risk that eviction changes will affect generation quality?
[09:22] Ravi: eviction only targets KV cache entries not prompt content; it may affect cached prefixes for long conversation flows but we expect quality impact to be minimal; we'll include quality checks in the bench.

--- Rapid-fire logistics ---
[10:00] Maya: ok let's call out owners — Ravi prepares PR with feature flag and e2e regression test, Diego runs rev replay and sanity checks in staging, Priya provisions Dedicated buffer and checks quotas, Lindsey circulates updated runbook and audit snippet, Maya sends Dedicated quote and timeline.
[10:20] Lindsey: I'll put the runbook into your incident doc and add a checklist with explicit timings and the SSO roles needed.
[10:28] Priya: on quotas — our cloud account will need vGPU quota bump; we'll start support ticket today.
[10:34] Diego: one more question, what about token-based throttling at the edge? could we have a policy to limit large-seq requests?
[10:40] Ravi: yes we have request shaping we can push to the edge, but that requires front-door integration. can be done as a short-term safety net.

--- Closing recap ---
[11:05] Maya: recap: action items assigned, bench 9/10 proposed, hotfix PR and feature flag by Ravi due 9/10, Dedicated pilot as backup, Lindsey to send runbook and audit stub 9/08, Maya to send pricing. agreed?
[11:20] Diego: agreed
[11:22] Markus: ok thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[11:25] Maya: thanks everyone we'll follow up in thread, end of call.

Note: transcript has minor transcription artifacts (names and acronyms sometimes mismatched).
